What a New Admin Has to Do

  • 1. Get a GCP project via ServiceNow + enable APIs + Claude models hours–days
  • 2. Provision inference WIF — keyless auth from GitHub to GCP (for calling Claude) (you run this) fullsend inference provision <org/repo> --project=<GCP_PROJECT> 2 min
  • 3. Get enrolled in the shared mint — keyless credential service: workflows prove identity, mint issues scoped tokens (ask in #forum-fullsend-ai) fullsend mint enroll <org/repo> --project=<MINT_PROJECT> ⚠ We're working on removing this step ask in Slack
  • 4. Set up GitHub — installs Apps, config repo, secrets, and enrolls repos (you run this) fullsend github setup <org> --mint-url=<MINT_URL> --inference-project=<GCP_PROJECT> --inference-wif-provider=<WIF> 5 min

Prereqs: fullsend CLI v0.13.0 · gh auth login · gcloud auth application-default login
GCP IAM: roles/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAdmin + roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin

Open the "New GCP Project" form — fill these fields:

Development (Lab, Sandbox...)

Usage of Google Vertex/Gemini API keys for coding assistance only

SEND-001 | fullsend

<rover-group>@redhat.com

Then configure your project following the installation docs.

Two Setup Modes

Per-Org Install
One setup covers the entire GitHub organization.
Creates .fullsend config repo
Installs GitHub Apps for all agent roles
Enroll repos with github enroll
Requires GitHub org owner 
fullsend github setup <org> \
  --mint-url=<MINT_URL> \
  --inference-project=<GCP_PROJECT> \
  --inference-wif-provider=<WIF>

End-user setup docs · Per-org reference

Per-Repo Install
Self-contained setup for a single repository.
No .fullsend config repo needed
Reuses existing shared Apps or creates new
Secrets and variables scoped to the repo
Only needs repo admin access 
fullsend github setup <org/repo> \
  --mint-url=<MINT_URL> \
  --inference-project=<GCP_PROJECT> \
  --inference-wif-provider=<WIF>
